narrative: Your law school application was denied because the model estimated an 82.9% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to lead to rejection. The most influential factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the fifth-to-sixth decile. This pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year class standing was the second most influential factor; at the second decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth decile, it also pushed toward failure, though less strongly. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor and the main one working in your favor: at 2.60 it is below the accepted average of 3.23, yet in this prediction it still pushed toward passing, just not enough to overcome the class-standing signals. Your gender and race were not used. To improve a future application, focus on strengthening the academic indicators that drove this result—especially sustained strong performance in advanced coursework—and consider retaking the LSAT, which was well below the accepted average, after targeted preparation. Speak with an admissions adviser about delaying reapplication until you have new evidence of readiness.
